title.zh: 卷120 志九十五 食货一 戸口田制
title.en: Volume 120 Treatises 95: Food and Money 1, Households and Land System
title.raw: 卷120 志九十五 食货一 戸口田制

sentences.zh: =志九十五= 食貨一 明末，苛政紛起，籌捐增餉，民窮財困。

translations.literal: =Treatise 95= Food and Money 1. At the end of the Ming, harsh policies arose one after another; fundraising levies and increased military provisions were imposed, and the people were impoverished while state finances were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 95: Food and Money, Part 1. In the closing years of the Ming, oppressive policies multiplied—special levies were raised and military allotments increased—until both the populace and the treasury were drained.

sentences.zh: 有清入主中國，概予蠲除，與民更始。

translations.literal: When the Qing entered and ruled China, they abolished these measures entirely and gave the people a fresh beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Qing assumed rule over China, they swept these burdens away wholesale and let the people begin anew.

translations.literal: By the eras of Kangxi and Qianlong, the state was rich and the people prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: By the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns, the empire was flush and the people at ease.

sentences.zh: 凡滋生人丁，永不加賦，又普免天下租稅，至再至三。

translations.literal: For all newly born population, taxation was never increased; moreover, land taxes throughout the empire were universally remitted, again and again.
translations.idiomatic: No matter how much the population grew, the poll tax was never raised; land taxes across the realm were remitted again and again—two and three times over.

translations.literal: Alas—such a thing had never existed in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Truly, nothing like it had been seen in all of history.

sentences.zh: 道、咸以降，海禁大開，國家多故。

translations.literal: From the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns onward, maritime prohibitions were greatly relaxed, and the state faced many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: After the Daoguang and Xianfeng periods, the maritime ban was largely lifted, and the dynasty was beset by one crisis after another.

sentences.zh: 耗財之途廣，而生財之道滯。

translations.literal: Paths for spending wealth widened, while means for generating wealth stagnated.
translations.idiomatic: Avenues for spending money multiplied, while ways of producing it stalled.

sentences.zh: 當軸者昧於中外大勢，召禍興戎，天府太倉之蓄，一旦蕩然，賠償兵費至四百餘兆。

translations.literal: Those in power were ignorant of the great trends at home and abroad; they invited disaster and raised armies. The reserves of the Heavenly Treasury and the Grand Granary were swept away in a single stroke, and military indemnities reached more than four hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: Men at the helm failed to grasp the larger forces shaping China and the world; they courted calamity and war until the imperial storehouses were emptied overnight and war reparations alone ran to more than four hundred million taels.

sentences.zh: 以中國所有財產抵借外債，積數十年不能清償。

translations.literal: Using all of China's wealth as collateral to borrow foreign debt, repayment could not be cleared even after decades.
translations.idiomatic: The nation's assets were pledged to service foreign loans, and decades of payments still could not clear the debt.

translations.literal: Apportionments and added levies were imposed; both the upper and lower levels were trapped in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Assessments were spread and surcharges piled on until court and country alike were squeezed dry.

sentences.zh: 乃改海運以節漕費，變圜法以行國幣，講鹽政以增歲入，開礦產以擴財源。

translations.literal: Thereupon they changed to sea transport to economize on grain-tribute shipping costs, altered the currency system to issue national coinage, reformed salt administration to increase annual revenue, and opened mineral resources to expand fiscal sources.
translations.idiomatic: The government turned to sea transport to cut grain-shipping costs, overhauled currency to put a national coinage in circulation, reworked the salt monopoly to swell annual receipts, and opened mines to broaden the revenue base.

sentences.zh: 以及創鐵路，改郵傳，設電局，通海舶。

translations.literal: Moreover they established railways, reformed the postal relay system, set up telegraph offices, and opened communication by seagoing vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Railways were built, the postal system modernized, telegraph bureaus established, and steam shipping brought into regular service.

sentences.zh: 新政繁興，孳孳謀利，而於古先聖王生眾食寡、為疾用舒之道，昧焉不講。

translations.literal: New policies proliferated, and they strove unceasingly to seek profit; yet regarding the way of the ancient sage-kings—to increase the people and reduce consumption, and to use resources sparingly in times of urgency—they were ignorant and did not discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: New policies multiplied and officials strained every nerve for gain, while the sage-kings' counsel—to swell the population, lighten consumption, and husband resources in haste—was left unheeded.

sentences.zh: 夫以唐、虞治平之世，而其告舜、禹也，諄諄以「四海困窮，天祿永終」為戒。

translations.literal: Consider—even in the well-governed age of Tang and Yu, in instructing Shun and Yu they earnestly took as a warning: "When the four seas are destitute, Heaven's blessings will end forever."
translations.idiomatic: Even in the golden age of Yao and Shun, their charge to Shun and Yu rang with one warning: "When the four seas are impoverished, Heaven's mandate is cut off forever."

translations.literal: Can those who hold a state possibly neglect this!
translations.idiomatic: How can any ruler of a realm afford to ignore this!

sentences.zh: 茲取清代理財始末，條著於篇。

translations.literal: Here we take the beginning and end of Qing fiscal administration and set them forth in sections within this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: What follows sets out the full arc of Qing revenue policy, arranged section by section.
